anomalies.observed: On the CAN BUS sheet, both MCP2515 controllers have their SPI data pins connected with the data lines reversed: U8 pin 14 (SI) is tied to net CAN_CIPO and pin 15 (SO) to net CAN_COPI, and U9 pin 14 (SI) is tied to CAN_CIPO with pin 15 (SO) to CAN_COPI. The CM4 side drives CAN_COPI (its MOSI output) onto the net that lands on the controllers' SO (output) pins, and reads CAN_CIPO (its MISO input) from the net that lands on the controllers' SI (input) pins.
anomalies.expected: Per the drawing's own SPI Naming Note (COPI = Controller Out, Peripheral In; CIPO = Controller In, Peripheral Out), the controller's SI pin must receive CAN_COPI and its SO pin must drive CAN_CIPO. This is exactly how the SC16IS752 UARTs are wired on the Serial sheet (U13 pin 11 SI = SERIAL_COPI, pin 12 SO = SERIAL_CIPO), so the CAN controllers are wired the opposite way.

evidence.quote: CAN BUS sheet, U8 MCP2515-xSO: left pins 14/15/16/13 carry red labels CAN_CIPO / CAN_COPI / CAN_CS0 / CAN_SCK (SI gets CIPO, SO gets COPI)
CAN BUS sheet, U9 MCP2515-xSO: pins 14/15/16/13 carry CAN_CIPO / CAN_COPI / CAN_CS1 / CAN_SCK (same reversal)
Power Control sheet SPI Naming Note: 'COPI "Controller Out, Peripheral In" CIPO "Controller In, Peripheral Out"'
Serial sheet U13 SC16IS752: pin 11 SI = SERIAL_COPI, pin 12 SO = SERIAL_CIPO (correct convention, for contrast)
two isolated CAN buses (CAN0, CAN1), each driven by its own MCP2515 SPI CAN controller (U8, U9)

anomalies.impact: MOSI and MISO are swapped on both SPI CAN controllers, producing contention on the CAN_COPI net (CM4 output vs. MCP2515 SO output) and floating inputs on the CAN_CIPO net (CM4 input vs. MCP2515 SI input). The SPI link to U8/U9 cannot communicate, so CAN0/CAN1 - the motor-control interface to the Odrive controllers - do not function.

parsed.summary: The drawing otherwise matches the documented reference design (16 MHz crystals, ideal-diode USB path, no GLOBAL_EN delay, PoE/e-stop quirks all as noted), but the SPI data lines to both MCP2515 CAN controllers are wired with MISO/MOSI swapped (SI tied to CAN_CIPO, SO to CAN_COPI), contrary to the board's own COPI/CIPO naming convention and to the correct UART wiring, which would break the CAN motor-control interface.
